papers.titleEn: Gradient-Engineered Hole-Selective Contact Layers via Spatially Confined Annealing for Efficient Tin-Lead and All-Perovskite Tandem Solar Cells
papers.abstract: Hole-selective contact layers (HSLs) govern charge extraction and interfacial energetics in perovskite solar cells, yet conventional designs are largely limited to planar architectures with homogeneous electronic properties. Such planar HSLs are insufficient for mixed tin-lead (Sn-Pb) perovskites, where short carrier diffusion lengths require efficient three-dimensional charge-collection pathways. Here, a spatially confined molecular-gradient engineering strategy is introduced to construct energetic-cascade HSLs within mesoporous frameworks. A screened and optimized phosphonic-acid self-assembled monolayer, [2-(7H-dibenzo[c,e]carbazol-7-yl)ethyl] phosphate, is incorporated into a mesoporous indium tin oxide nanocrystal matrix. Spatially confined annealing drives directional molecular redistribution, generating a controllable bottom-to-surface concentration gradient. This gradient establishes continuous energy cascades and graded hole-transport channels, while simultaneously modulating the crystallization of the overlying Sn-Pb perovskite to suppress nonradiative recombination. Single-junction Sn-Pb perovskite solar cells achieve a power conversion efficiency of 24.14%, and monolithic two-terminal all-perovskite tandem solar cells reach 29.56% efficiency with substantially improved operational stability. More broadly, this work establishes molecular-gradient engineering in porous matrices as a versatile strategy for programming charge transport and interfacial chemistry in solution-processed optoelectronic devices.
papers.filename: Weijun Ke, Adv. Mater., 2026, Gradient-Engineered Hole-Selective Contact Layers via Spatially Confined Annealing for Efficient Tin-Lead and All-Perovskite Tandem Solar Cells

papers.titleEn: Enhanced Molecular-Structure Dual-Recognition by Enzyme-Embedded Metal-Phenolic Networks for Wearable Plant Sensing of Pesticides
papers.abstract: On‐site monitoring of plant health using enzyme‐based wearable sensors is essential for sustainable agriculture, yet inherent enzyme instability and poor molecular recognition remain major obstacles. Here, we present a robust plant‐wearable hydrogel sensor based on an acetylcholinesterase‐embedded metal‐phenolic network (AChE@MPN) to overcome these limitations through a dual‐recognition strategy, markedly improving stability and selectivity relative to conventional sensors. The MPN protects the enzyme's native conformation, maintaining catalytic kinetics comparable to those of the free enzyme. Within this architecture, the dual‐recognition strategy integrates metal‐assisted adsorption with enzymatic recognition, engaging pesticide molecules through synergistic P‐O‐Zr coordination, hydrogen bonding, and π–π stacking to yield a 1.41‐fold higher response to phoxim than that obtained with free AChE. Notably, the AChE@MPN exhibits an approximately 88‐fold higher binding affinity for phoxim than for its nonaromatic analog malathion, indicating that the signal gain originates from selective enrichment. These features enable the sensor to discriminate phoxim from interfering substances, with a limit of detection of 2 ng mL −1 , and to perform on‐site monitoring of phoxim degradation on living tomato plants. This dual‐recognition design offers a general strategy for pesticide monitoring and may inspire plant‐sensing innovations for sustainable agriculture.
papers.filename: Xu Yan, Adv. Mater., 2026, Enhanced Molecular-Structure Dual-Recognition by Enzyme-Embedded Metal-Phenolic Networks for Wearable Plant Sensing of Pesticides

papers.titleEn: Light-Mediated Electrification in Interface-Engineered Quasi-2D Perovskite Triboelectric Nanogenerators for Self-Powered Data Encoding
papers.abstract: Light-mediated electrification enables triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) to respond to both mechanical and optical stimuli, offering opportunities for self-powered optical sensing and information encoding. However, achieving stable and distinguishable electrical contrast between dark and illuminated states remains challenging due to inefficient carrier separation, interfacial recombination, and unstable surface-charge accumulation. Here, we demonstrate an interface-engineered quasi-2D perovskite-based TENG for enhanced light-mediated electrification and self-powered data encoding. A self-assembled monolayer is introduced on the hole transport layer to regulate interfacial energetics and improve perovskite film quality. The resulting interfacial modification facilitates hole extraction, reduces trap-state density, suppresses charge recombination, and promotes photogenerated electron accumulation near the triboelectric surface. Consequently, the modified TENG exhibits significantly enhanced light-mediated output, with peak-to-peak voltage and current increases of 142.55% and 145.62%, respectively. The amplified dark/light contrast enables direct binary discrimination without external amplification. By converting light-modulated voltage waveforms into binary sequences, self-powered ASCII encoding is demonstrated for uppercase letters, numerical digits, and selected symbols. This work establishes interface engineering as an effective strategy for enhancing photo-triboelectric coupling and advancing light-controlled, self-powered information encoding.
papers.filename: Yuljae Cho, Small, 2026, Light-Mediated Electrification in Interface-Engineered Quasi-2D Perovskite Triboelectric Nanogenerators for Self-Powered Data Encoding
